title: The Lighter Brief
overview: A pretty easygoing edition. Grand Theft Auto VI finally landed with a who's who of musicians inside, Ice Spice met her wax twin in Times Square, and Charlotte opened its first new wastewater plant in nearly 50 years. There's also some community kindness around Thanksgiving food, a big award win for a Jamaican building, and a couple of health stories worth knowing about.

stories.headline: GTA VI is out, and half the music world is in it
stories.summary: After 13 years, Grand Theft Auto VI was released at midnight on Nov. 19, and Billboard reports it has already pulled in almost $4 billion in sales. Its radio stations are hosted by stars like Bad Bunny, Gloria Estefan, Lana Del Rey and Charlamagne tha God, and some artists appear in the game itself. One viral moment: streamer iShowSpeed ran into Sexyy Red dancing in an in-game nightclub. Not everyone is a fan, though. Rep. Tim Burchett (R-Tenn.) told TMZ that parents who let kids play it are making a bad call.
key_facts: Released Nov. 19, 13 years after the previous main installment
Almost $4 billion in sales so far, per Billboard
Radio hosts include Bad Bunny, Anitta, Burna Boy, TLC's Chilli and Gucci Mane
Sexyy Red reposted the viral clip, joking: "We was just chillin mane."
disputed: The sales figure comes from Billboard's report; the articles don't cite an official breakdown from Rockstar.
Rep. Burchett's criticism is his opinion, given to TMZ.
stories.why: It's one of the biggest entertainment launches in years, and a fun showcase of music from Afrobeats to classical.

stories.headline: Colts release Charlotte native QB Daniel Jones
stories.summary: The Indianapolis Colts released quarterback Daniel Jones on Nov. 20, a day after a 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans. Jones, who played at Charlotte Latin and Duke, has had a rough season, leading the NFL in interceptions. He'll go on waivers, and teams like the Patriots or Ravens could look at signing him afterward.
key_facts: Jones went 3-8 as a starter this season with 7 touchdowns and 13 interceptions
He signed a two-year, $88 million extension with $60 million guaranteed, which the Colts still owe
Anthony Richardson is expected to take over as the Colts' starter
The Colts' next game is Nov. 29
disputed: ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported that some people in the Colts building believed Jones wanted out and might have asked for his release soon. Coach Shane Steichen said Jones never requested to be released.
stories.why: It's a big local sports story for Charlotte, and Jones may get a fresh start somewhere else.

stories.headline: Charlotte food share helps families gear up for Thanksgiving
stories.summary: Nourish Up handed out bags of turkey and fixings at a pop-up food share in Charlotte, and more people signed up than ever before. Families said high grocery, gas and rent costs have made this year tough, and the help means a real holiday meal. The organization is welcoming donations, and a few spots may still open up next week.
key_facts: Nourish Up has served 3,700 people so far, about 100 more than this time last year
It runs 40 food bank locations in Mecklenburg County
Most-needed donations: canned fruit, canned pasta, cooking oil and butter
Donations are accepted at its north Charlotte warehouse
stories.why: If you'd like to help a neighbor this Thanksgiving, or need a little help yourself, this is a concrete way to do it.

stories.headline: Montego Bay's The Pinnacle makes Jamaican history with four design awards
stories.summary: The Pinnacle in Montego Bay is the first Jamaican project to win at the Americas Property Awards, and it took home four of them. The awards were presented at a ceremony at The Ritz-Carlton, South Beach in Miami, and the news was also announced at Design Week JA 2026.
key_facts: Wins: Hotel Architecture, Mixed Use Architecture, Mixed Use Development, and Residential High-Rise Architecture
Developed by LCH Developments with Accor Ennismore
Submitted by DesignHQ
stories.why: It's a proud first for Jamaican architecture on an international stage.

stories.headline: Health officials flag rising antibiotic resistance in the Americas
stories.summary: The Pan American Health Organization says resistance to carbapenems, a group of 'last line' antibiotics used when other treatments fail, has risen steadily over the past decade across the Americas, including the Caribbean. That makes some serious hospital infections harder to treat, and it can also make common ones like urinary tract infections harder to treat. PAHO is calling for better surveillance, infection prevention, access to new antibiotics, and careful use of the ones we have.
key_facts: Carbapenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae rose from about 15% in 2015 to 26% in 2024
In E. coli, it rose from 3% to 5%
Median resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii hit 77% in 2024 across the seven countries reporting
The data were released for World AMR Awareness Week, Nov. 18–24
disputed: These are regional surveillance figures, based on data from a limited number of countries (13 to 15 for the main bacteria, seven for Acinetobacter). PAHO itself says surveillance needs to expand.
stories.why: Using antibiotics only when they're needed, and as prescribed, helps keep them working for everyone.

stories.headline: South American football backs Infantino for another FIFA term
stories.summary: CONMEBOL, the 10-country South American football body, says it 'unanimously' supports Gianni Infantino's re-election as FIFA president. He also has support from Africa and Asia, but for the first time he faces challengers: France's Philippe Diallo and Japan's Kozo Tashima. Infantino has drawn criticism over a dropped plan to allow private investment in the World Cup.
key_facts: The vote is March 18 in Rabat
211 member federations vote, and a winner needs at least 106
UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin backs Diallo
Tashima is campaigning on transparency and integrity
stories.why: It's the first genuinely contested FIFA presidential race in years, and it will shape how world football is run.

stories.headline: Ice Spice meets her wax twin in Times Square
stories.summary: Madame Tussauds New York unveiled an Ice Spice wax figure on Nov. 19, and the Bronx rapper was briefly left speechless at how accurate it was. The figure recreates her early-career look: copper curls, a red tiger-print catsuit donated from her own wardrobe, and Black Air Jordan 4s. She joked that they even nailed her forehead.
key_facts: On display at Madame Tussauds' Times Square location into 2027
Includes a replica of a bracelet Doja Cat gave her
Ice Spice is 26; her only 2026 release so far is "Out My Face (My Baby)" with Lil Yachty
stories.why: It's a fun, feel-good career milestone, and something to see if you're in NYC.

stories.headline: Trump holds a 90-minute press conference after his Asia trip
stories.summary: President Trump held a wide-ranging White House news conference lasting almost 90 minutes on Friday. It followed his recent Asia trip, which included announced trade deals and a three-way meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. The articles provided don't give much detail on what was said.
key_facts: The news conference ran almost 90 minutes
The Asia trip included trade deal announcements
It also included a trilateral meeting with Xi and Putin, which The Hill described as more controversial
stories.why: The Asia trip's trade deals and diplomacy could shape U.S. relations with China and Russia going forward.
